overview:
Summer Lee enters the general election as a heavy favorite in a Pittsburgh-area district that leans Democratic by about ten points. She has raised roughly $1.6 million and holds about $1.7 million in cash on hand, while Republican James Hayes has raised under $65,000 and reported only about $2,500 in the bank. No independent spending against her has been reported, and prediction markets price her win chances near 98 percent.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the fundraising gap, and the advantages of incumbency. Those all point to a comfortable double-digit Democratic margin. The race would draw attention only if national conditions shifted sharply or outside money arrived late on the Republican side; neither has appeared so far.
